findings.description: offset = page * PAGE_SIZE with a 1-based page skips the first page of results; page 1 returns rows 21-40.
findings.scenario: list_orders(conn, 1, page=1) returns offset 20, so the customer's 20 most recent orders are never returned; a customer with <=20 orders gets an empty list.

findings.description: status from the request query string is interpolated into the SQL via % formatting.
findings.scenario: status="x' OR '1'='1" returns all orders; status="x' UNION SELECT ..." can exfiltrate other data.
findings.fix: sql = "SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE status = ?"; conn.execute(sql, (status,))

findings.description: cancel_order takes customer_id but never checks that the order belongs to that customer; it looks up and updates by order_id only.
findings.scenario: Logged-in customer 5 calls cancel_order(conn, order_id=<customer 9's order>, customer_id=5) and cancels another customer's order.
findings.fix: Include customer_id in both the SELECT and UPDATE: WHERE id = ? AND customer_id = ?.

findings.description: Check-then-act: status is read, then updated in a separate statement without a status guard, so an order that ships in between can still be cancelled. Also, orders already cancelled/delivered are treated as cancellable (only 'shipped' is excluded).
findings.scenario: Order is 'pending' at SELECT, another process sets it to 'shipped', then this UPDATE sets it to 'cancelled'. Or a 'delivered' order gets set to 'cancelled'.
findings.fix: Single atomic statement: UPDATE orders SET status='cancelled' WHERE id=? AND customer_id=? AND status IN ('pending','paid'); return cursor.rowcount > 0.

findings.description: with_retry retries any callable on OperationalError, including writes; also sleeps after the final failed attempt for no reason, and raises None-typed error if attempts <= 0.
findings.scenario: with_retry(lambda: cancel_order(...)) with a lock error after a partial write is re-run; with attempts=0, `raise last` raises TypeError (raise None).
findings.fix: Only retry idempotent operations or roll back before retry; skip the sleep after the last attempt; validate attempts >= 1.

findings.description: direction is hardcoded and ordering on created_at/total_cents is not unique, so paginated results can duplicate or skip rows across pages when values tie.
findings.scenario: Two orders share the same created_at; they may swap order between page 1 and page 2 queries.
findings.fix: Add a tie-breaker: ORDER BY {column} {direction}, id {direction}.
